overall_reason: The 20-day TSLA candlestick chart has even $20 ticks, trading-day spacing that skips the 3 April holiday, a peak that matches its caption ('4/17 high $409') and a last close that matches the $373.72 headline.

score.reason: T-CHART-FORM, T-HONEST-SCALE, T-CHART-TEXT-MATCH and T-STAT-TILE pass on the candlestick chart and the price tile, with the takeaway in the caption as print expects (C53); it loses points because the chart has no source line (DVZ-010) and its up and down colours differ only in tone.

findings.where: html > body > figure > svg (近期价格走势), 794 (contact sheet #1, 673 by 266px at y432; tiles/794-00.png)
findings.evidence: The figure has a caption with the takeaway ('图 1. TSLA 近 20 个交易日走势(3/26 - 4/23)。4/17 冲高 $409 后回落, 财报后因 capex 指引下跌。'), but no source line names where the prices come from. The charts table `near` has a caption and no source. The y axis also has no unit (`unit` null): the ticks read 320 to 420 with no '$'.
findings.before: A price chart with a caption and no data source or unit.
findings.after: Add a source line under the caption ('数据来源: [DATA NEEDED: price data provider], 日线收盘') and put '$' on the top tick or in the axis title.
findings.why: A research note's reader checks where a price series came from before acting on it. On a Read figure a source line is expected.

findings.evidence: Rising candles are navy #1b365d and falling candles grey #6b6a64, both filled. On the grayscale contact sheet they show as dark grey against mid grey. They stay apart, but only by tone.
findings.before: Up and down told apart by fill tone alone.
findings.after: Draw rising candles hollow (outline only) and falling candles filled. This is the usual print convention, and it survives photocopying.
findings.why: A print report gets copied in black and white, where two filled tones can merge.

strengths: The candlestick chart is the right form for daily price ranges. Its ticks run in even $20 steps from 320 to 420 (`even_value_steps` true), and the axis does not start at zero, which is correct for a price range.

The marks match the words. There are 20 candles for '20 trading days', 4/3 (a market holiday) is skipped in the spacing, the tallest wick sits on 4/17 near $409, and the last candle closes near $374 against the $373.72 headline.
Both financial tables right-align all their figures (14 of 14 and 8 of 8) and use '--' for missing values rather than leaving gaps.
The price tile gives its date ('2026.04.23 收盘') and a signed change ('财报后 -3.56%') in neutral grey, not in colour alone.
